A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same CamTrol work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. External videos and supplementary materials mentioned in the PDFs were not accessed.

before.justification: V2 reports original video-generation experiments, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1 and 3, and a depth-optimization ablation in Appendix A.4.

after.justification: V3 reports original quantitative and qualitative generation results, computational measurements in Tables 2 and 4, and timestep sensitivity results in Table 3.

M1.justification: The core point-cloud reconstruction, depth optimization, noise initialization and denoising procedure retain Eqs. (1)–(5). Appendix B and Table 5 add an optional reference-video input route using SfM to estimate the requested camera trajectory. The new pseudocode and rotation details otherwise elaborate existing operations.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix A.3 evaluates eight basic motions using 1,000 samples with UCF-101 prompts and reference videos; this distinct quantitative coverage is absent from v3, which retains RealEstate10k evaluation. V3 also adds an explicit same-scene, multiple-trajectory generation demonstration in Figure 9.

E2.justification: MotionCtrl and CameraCtrl remain the principal competitors. V3 adds vanilla SVD to the quantitative and qualitative comparisons, while AnimateDiff disappears from the reported comparisons, including those previously in v2 Appendix A.3. The added ground-truth Reference row calibrates motion metrics rather than representing another competing method.

E3.justification: The main evaluation changes from 51 RealEstate10k trajectories paired with ten MotionCtrl prompts each to 500 randomly sampled prompt-trajectory pairs. V3 introduces computational evaluations at two resolutions, a quantitative t0 sweep, and CogVideoX-2B testing at 720 × 480 with 49 frames. The principal metrics and stated 25 diffusion steps remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds numerical timestep sensitivity at t0 = 5, 10 and 15, quantitative comparison against uncontrolled SVD, and CogVideoX generalization examples. It removes v2's controlled depth-optimization ablation in Appendix A.4/Table 4. The original qualitative prompt-only, layout-prior and timestep analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V3's ground-truth motion-metric reference is a calibration control, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1's results are replaced under the revised sampling protocol, so absolute score differences do not establish same-setting gains. V2 places CamTrol best or tied across all metrics; v3 reports best FVD but CameraCtrl has better FID (67.59 versus 68.06) and CLIP-SIM (0.3138 versus 0.3110). V3 adds runtime, memory and numerical timestep results, while omitting the earlier UCF-101 and depth-ablation tables.

T1.justification: V3 Appendix F introduces Eq. (6), explicitly defining the rotation trajectory and its radius through mean depth in a central image patch. V2 describes camera extrinsics generically without this mathematical specification. Eqs. (1)–(5) remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V3's abstract, introduction and conclusion explicitly claim superior video quality and motion alignment against finetuned methods, whereas v2's corresponding summaries emphasize effectiveness and robustness. The central training-free contribution and claims about generalization, complex trajectories, scalable motion and 3D rotation remain substantially the same.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive discussion of point clouds versus Gaussian splatting, sequential rendering costs, the relationship between static RealEstate10k references and FVD, and motion-blur failure conditions and possible remedies. These extend v2's fidelity-diversity and dataset-generalization discussion. The new Figure 2 depicts the timestep tradeoff in the opposite direction to the retained prose in Sections 3.2 and 4.3.

D1.justification: V3 adds checkpoint links, inpainting steps, guidance defaults, resolution handling, frame and decoding settings, 6-fps reference processing, computational-test settings, Algorithm 1 and the rotation-center construction. Much of this newly documents previously underspecified operations rather than establishing changed settings. Conversely, v2's explicit identification of DDIM as the scheduler is dropped.

R1.justification: V3 adds CogVideoX and a substantive comparison with 3D Gaussian Splatting, plus a COLMAP pointer. References to Blended Diffusion, DDIM and UCF-101 are removed. The main positioning around camera control, latent-noise priors and video models for 3D generation remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental settings, comparison narrative and contribution summaries are substantially rewritten. The former A.1–A.5 appendix is reorganized into Appendices A–G, with dedicated implementation, representation-choice, rotation and motion-blur discussions replacing much of the gallery-oriented structure. Much of the introduction, related work and core method prose is retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds a distribution-transition diagram, a multi-trajectory illustration, computational tables, a timestep table and an algorithm display. It replaces the main qualitative comparison, revises the backbone examples and expands Table 1 with control rows. The opening gallery and most appendix montages disappear, while the pipeline and several qualitative ablations are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the core evaluation and implementation more assessable through vanilla-SVD and ground-truth controls, concrete reproduction details, resource measurements and numerical timestep analysis. It also identifies specific motion-blur limitations. These gains are tempered by losing the UCF-101 comparison and depth-optimization ablation. Broad superiority claims remain stronger than Table 1's mixed quality rankings, and the new Figure 2 conflicts with the prose about timestep effects, limiting the overall improvement.
